rationale: normalizeEmailList accepts a string and splits on [,\n], lowercasing/deduping. A string instead of array must be tolerated (normalized to 3 emails), not rejected with 500. Confirms lenient coercion of the pilot allowlist.

title: PAN embedded in pilotUserEmails governance allowlist
rationale: Free-text governance field could capture a card number. A PCI-aware system rejects with a payment-card message; if no PCI filter exists here the value is merely normalized (200) and stored as a benign string. The test surfaces whether calendar governance scrubs PAN-like input; a 500 is a defect.

title: Start Outlook OAuth connection when Entra/Graph not configured (parked)
rationale: startOutlookConnection calls requireConfiguredOutlook; with MICROSOFT_ENTRA_* unset the deployed env throws CalendarIntegrationUnavailableError -> serviceUnavailableResponse (503). Confirms the Outlook integration is gracefully parked, not 500/200.

title: List Outlook calendars while integration is parked
rationale: listOutlookCalendars -> requireConfiguredOutlook + ensureActorCanUseOutlookCalendar both raise CalendarIntegrationUnavailableError when unconfigured -> 503. Parked-boundary check on the calendars listing endpoint.

title: Sync event with empty body (no sourceModule/sourceRecordId/eventType)
expectMessageContains: sourcemodule, sourcerecordid, and eventtype are required
rationale: http.ts validates the body shape (sourceModule in {leads,training}, string sourceRecordId, string eventType) and returns 400 BEFORE the service's 503 gate. Empty body fails all three checks.

title: Sync event with invalid sourceModule value
expectMessageContains: sourcemodule, sourcerecordid, and eventtype are required
rationale: The contract restricts sync sourceModule to 'leads'|'training'; http.ts rejects 'consignment' even though it is a valid calendar source module elsewhere. This 400 happens before the Outlook-config 503, so it is deterministic.

title: Sync event with numeric sourceRecordId (wrong type)
expectMessageContains: sourcemodule, sourcerecordid, and eventtype are required
rationale: http.ts checks `typeof body.sourceRecordId !== 'string'`; a number fails the guard and returns 400 before any service call. Type-mismatch boundary.

title: Sync event missing eventType field
expectMessageContains: sourcemodule, sourcerecordid, and eventtype are required
rationale: `typeof body.eventType !== 'string'` is true when omitted -> 400 in http.ts. Required-field check on eventType, independent of the parked 503.

title: Sync valid-shaped lead discovery event while integration parked
rationale: Body shape passes http.ts validation, so the request reaches syncCalendarEventToOutlook -> requireConfiguredOutlook, which throws CalendarIntegrationUnavailableError (503) when Entra/Graph is unset. Confirms the sync path is parked behind the same boundary once shape is valid.

title: Sync lead with non-discovery eventType (only discovery_call allowed for leads)
rationale: eventType 'consignment_audit' is a valid enum (passes the string check in http.ts), so it reaches the service. If Outlook were configured, resolveCalendarEventForSync throws 'Only discovery_call events are supported for lead calendar sync' (400). When parked, requireConfiguredOutlook short-circuits to 503 first. Either proves leads are restricted to discovery_call; a correct system never 200s/500s here.

title: Script/HTML injection in sourceRecordId on sync
rationale: A non-empty string passes http.ts shape validation; the value is record-scoped via Prisma findFirst (parameterized), so it can only resolve to a nonexistent lead. When parked the 503 gate fires first; if configured it would be 'Lead calendar event not found' (mapped to 400/404). Must never be 500 — confirms the script payload is handled as inert data.

title: Sync training event for a well-formed but nonexistent record id
rationale: Valid shape -> service. When parked, 503 fires at requireConfiguredOutlook. If configured, resolveCalendarEventForSync's record-scoped findFirst returns null -> 'Training calendar event not found' (mapped to badRequest/404). Proves IDOR-safe not-found handling, never 200 for an unknown id.

title: Use the rejected per-event path /calendar/outlook/events/:eventId
rationale: matchPath('/calendar/outlook/events/:eventId') unconditionally returns badRequestResponse steering callers to the /sync endpoint, regardless of method or id. Confirms the legacy per-id route is closed off (no direct event mutation by id).

title: Wrong HTTP method on workspace (POST instead of GET)
rationale: http.ts returns methodNotAllowedResponse(res, method, ['GET']) for any non-GET on /calendar/workspace. Method-guard edge.

title: Wrong HTTP method on outlook connect (GET instead of POST)
rationale: /calendar/outlook/connect only accepts POST; GET hits methodNotAllowedResponse(['POST']). Confirms method allow-list before the 503 config gate.

title: Disconnect Outlook connection (DELETE) when integration disabled
rationale: disconnectOutlookConnection short-circuits: when config.outlookCalendar.enabled is false it returns buildConnectionSummary(null,false) with 200 (idempotent no-op), never erroring. Confirms disconnect is safe/idempotent even with no connection and a parked integration. Safe: only touches the caller's own (nonexistent) connection.

title: Disconnect Outlook connection twice (repeat DELETE)
rationale: disconnectOutlookConnection returns a 200 connection summary whether or not a connection row exists (findUnique null -> early return). A repeated DELETE must remain a 200 no-op, proving idempotency with no 404/500. Safe: targets only the caller's own connection.

title: Update Outlook connection settings (PATCH) while parked
rationale: updateOutlookConnection calls requireConfiguredOutlook first; when Entra/Graph env is unset it throws CalendarIntegrationUnavailableError -> 503. Confirms connection-settings write is parked behind config, before touching the (nonexistent) connection.

title: Update Outlook connection with invalid meetingProvider enum while parked
rationale: http.ts forwards meetingProvider verbatim into updateOutlookConnection, which hits requireConfiguredOutlook (503) before toMeetingProviderPreference would normalize it. When parked the deterministic result is 503; the case still proves an invalid enum never yields 500 or silent acceptance.

title: OAuth callback with no code/state/error params
rationale: The callback is unauthenticated and on missing params returns a 302 redirect to /calendar?outlook=error with 'Missing Outlook authorization code or state'. With Entra/Graph unset, requireConfiguredOutlook throws first -> 503. Either way it must not 500; confirms callback degrades to redirect or parked-503, never crashes on empty params.

title: Add cart item with missing presentationId
rationale: loadVisibleDealerCatalogPresentation trims body.presentationId; undefined/empty trims to '' and throws 'Product presentation id is required'. The http catch (no 'not found' substring) routes to badRequestResponse -> 400. Proves required-field enforcement on the cart-add path.

title: Add cart item with whitespace-only presentationId
rationale: presentationId.trim() yields '' for a whitespace string, hitting the same explicit 'Product presentation id is required' guard. Confirms trimming is applied before the empty check, not just a falsy check.

title: Add cart item with well-formed but nonexistent presentationId
rationale: A non-existent presentation is rejected by the snapshot/visible-catalog resolution with 'Product presentation is not visible in the active/current dealer catalog'. That message lacks the 'not found' substring, so the http catch returns 400 (badRequestResponse), NOT 404 — the server never trusts a client presentation id and treats unknown==not-visible.

title: Add cart item with SQL injection string as presentationId
rationale: Prisma parameterizes the id lookup, so the injection string is treated as a literal id that matches no visible presentation -> 'not visible' -> 400. Must NOT 500 and must not execute SQL; proves safe handling of hostile text in the id field.

title: Add cart item with quantity 0 (below min, gets clamped)
rationale: clampDealerPortalQuantity does Math.min(Math.max(trunc(0),1),1_000_000) = 1. The server silently clamps 0 up to the min of 1 rather than rejecting, so a correct system returns 201 with a quantity of 1. Documents the deliberate clamp-not-reject design at the lower boundary.

title: Add cart item with negative quantity (clamped to 1)
rationale: clampDealerPortalQuantity Math.max(trunc(-50),1)=1, so a negative quantity is clamped to 1 and the line is created -> 201. Confirms a negative qty can never persist; the resulting cart line quantity must be 1, never negative.

title: Add cart item with quantity above max (clamped to 1,000,000)
rationale: DEALER_PORTAL_MAX_LINE_QUANTITY is 1_000_000; clamp caps 99,999,999 to 1,000,000 and creates the line -> 201. Proves the upper quantity bound is enforced by clamping, and the stored quantity should equal exactly 1,000,000.

title: Add cart item with non-numeric quantity (NaN -> clamped to 1)
rationale: clampDealerPortalQuantity: !Number.isFinite('abc' coerced) returns 1. A non-numeric quantity is normalized to 1 rather than 500/400 — confirms the Number.isFinite guard prevents a NaN quantity from ever being persisted.

title: Add cart item with fractional quantity (truncated)
rationale: Math.trunc(2.9)=2 then clamped within bounds -> line created with quantity 2 -> 201. Verifies fractional quantities are floored via truncation, not rounded or rejected; stored quantity must be an integer 2.

title: Add same presentation twice merges onto one line (quantity sums)
rationale: addCurrentDealerPortalCartItem merges onto the existing line for the same baseProductId (quantity = clamp(existing+new)) rather than creating a duplicate line. Running this twice must yield ONE line, not two — proves per-product idempotent merge and no duplicate-line growth.

title: Add cart item with payment card number (PAN) in lineNote
rationale: lineNote is free text persisted on the order line. A correct system must reject a Luhn-valid PAN (assertNoRawPaymentCardData / containsLikelyPaymentCardNumber pattern) per the PCI boundary guard. NOTE: dealer-portal/service.ts does NOT currently call the PCI guard on lineNote, so a live 201 here flags a real PCI gap the harness should surface.

title: Add cart item with 10,000-char lineNote
rationale: optionalDealerPortalText only trims lineNote with no length cap in the dealer-portal code, so a 10k note is accepted (201). 400 is allowed only if a DB column length or upstream limit truncates/rejects. Probes whether any max-length bound exists on the free-text note.

title: Add cart item with emoji/unicode lineNote
rationale: lineNote is opaque trimmed text; emoji and multibyte unicode must round-trip cleanly and persist -> 201. Must not 500 on multibyte handling; verifies UTF-8 safety of the free-text path.

title: Add cart item as TERRITORY_MANAGER (no dealer_portal module)
rationale: ROLE_DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS for TERRITORY_MANAGER excludes 'dealer_portal'; assertModuleAccess throws AuthorizationError -> forbiddenResponse 403. Confirms internal sales roles cannot enter the dealer self-service ordering surface.

title: Add cart item as EXECUTIVE (has module + order_view but not order_create)
rationale: EXECUTIVE has the dealer_portal module and dealer.order_view, but ROLE_DEFAULT_ACTION_ACCESS grants it NO dealer.order_create. The action gate (assertActionAccess 'dealer.order_create') throws -> 403. Tests the action-level (vs module-level) RBAC boundary — read role denied on a write.

title: View dealer cart as FINANCE (no dealer_portal module)
rationale: FINANCE module list omits 'dealer_portal'; the GET /me/cart handler calls requireAuthenticatedActor with module dealer_portal and assertModuleAccess inside getCurrentDealerPortalCart both deny -> 403. Confirms even read access to the dealer cart is gated to portal roles.

title: Update cart line with nonexistent lineId
rationale: updateCurrentDealerPortalCartItem finds the line in the caller's own cart; a missing id throws 'Cart line not found'. That message contains 'not found', so the http catch routes to notFoundResponse -> 404. Also proves a line id from another cart cannot be addressed.

title: Delete cart line with malformed (non-UUID) lineId
rationale: lineId is matched against in-memory cart.lines by string equality (no UUID format validation), so a malformed id simply matches nothing -> 'Cart line not found' -> 404. 400 acceptable if id-shape validation is added. Must not 500 on a malformed path segment.

title: Update cart line quantity to 0 (clamped to 1, not deletion)
rationale: Line-resolution happens before quantity clamping, so a 0 quantity on a nonexistent line still yields 'Cart line not found' (404). On a real line, quantity 0 would clamp to 1 (not remove the line) — confirming update never zero-deletes. Here the line-not-found path dominates and proves ordering of checks.

title: Submit order with missing poNumber
rationale: submitCurrentDealerPortalOrder requires body.poNumber?.trim(); undefined -> '' -> throws 'A purchase order (PO) number is required to submit a dealer order' -> 400. Confirms PO is a hard precondition for the DRAFT->SUBMITTED transition.

title: Submit order with whitespace-only poNumber
rationale: poNumber.trim() collapses whitespace to '' which is falsy -> same required-PO rejection -> 400. Proves the PO check is trim-based, blocking a blank-but-present PO from satisfying the requirement.

title: Submit order with valid PO but empty cart
rationale: After the PO check, submit asserts cart.lineCount>=1 && cart.lines.length>=1, else throws 'Add at least one product to your cart before submitting an order' -> 400. Note: harness must NOT pre-seed the cart for this case. Proves an empty draft cannot be submitted even with a PO.

title: Submit order with shipToLocationId that belongs to another account
rationale: assertDealerPortalShipToBelongsToAccount looks up AccountLocation by {id, accountId=portalUser.accountId}; a foreign/unknown location returns null -> 'Ship-to location does not belong to this dealer account' -> 400. Enforces portal isolation on the ship-to derived from the caller's own account, never client-trusted.

title: Submit order with PAN in order notes
rationale: The order 'notes' field is persisted free text. A correct system must reject a Luhn-valid PAN per the PCI boundary guard. submitCurrentDealerPortalOrder does NOT call assertNoRawPaymentCardData on notes, so a live 201 here flags a real PCI storage gap; the expected correct behavior is rejection.

title: Submit order as SALES_BD_REP (no dealer_portal module)
rationale: SALES_BD_REP has the internal 'orders' module and order.* actions but NOT 'dealer_portal' nor dealer.order_submit. requireAuthenticatedActor(module dealer_portal, action dealer.order_submit) denies -> 403. Confirms internal order permissions do not cross into the dealer self-service submit path.

title: Re-submit an already-submitted order (double submit)
rationale: Submit advances the single DRAFT cart to SUBMITTED via an atomic updateMany guarded on status=DRAFT && source=DEALER_SELF_SERVICE && lineCount>=1. After a first successful submit there is no DRAFT cart, so a second submit matches 0 rows -> 'This order was already submitted; reload your cart and try again' -> 400 (when run back-to-back after a seeded+submitted cart). Proves the DRAFT->SUBMITTED transition is one-shot and double-click safe.

title: Get dealer order detail by nonexistent orderId
rationale: getCurrentDealerPortalOrder findFirst is scoped to {accountId=own, source=DEALER_SELF_SERVICE, status != DRAFT}; an unknown id returns null and the http layer returns notFoundResponse(DealerPortalOrder) -> 404. Also confirms a DRAFT (un-submitted) cart id is not retrievable via the orders detail endpoint.

title: List dealer orders as REGIONAL_DIRECTOR (no dealer_portal module)
rationale: REGIONAL_DIRECTOR module access omits 'dealer_portal'; assertModuleAccess in getCurrentDealerPortalOrders denies before any data read -> 403. Confirms the dealer order history is isolated from oversight roles that lack the portal module.

title: Get dealer catalog as TRAINING_OPS (no dealer_portal module)
rationale: getCurrentDealerPortalCatalog calls assertModuleAccess(role,'dealer_portal'); TRAINING_OPS lacks that module -> 403. Verifies the dealer-scoped catalog (a different, snapshot-filtered view than the internal product catalog) is not exposed to internal training staff.

title: Favorite a nonexistent/not-visible presentation
rationale: favoriteCurrentDealerPortalProduct resolves the presentation via loadVisibleDealerCatalogPresentation, which rejects an unknown id with 'not visible in the active/current dealer catalog' (lacks 'not found') -> 400. Confirms favorites can only target presentations actually visible in the dealer's catalog snapshot, not arbitrary ids.

title: Submit order with script payload in notes (XSS-safe storage)
rationale: notes is opaque trimmed text; a script payload must be stored/escaped as inert text, never executed or cause a 500. A seeded non-empty cart yields 201 with the literal string persisted; 400 only if an input sanitizer rejects it. Proves safe handling of HTML/script in the free-text notes field. (Harness must seed one cart line first.)

title: Add cart item with malformed JSON body
rationale: readJsonBody JSON.parse fails on the trailing-comma/empty-value body and throws 'Invalid JSON body: ...'; the http catch routes to badRequestResponse -> 400. Confirms the body parser rejects malformed JSON cleanly rather than 500-ing on parse failure.

title: Create voice note with neither transcript nor audio
expectMessageContains: requires either a transcript or an audio file
rationale: createMobileVoiceNote throws 'Voice note requires either a transcript or an audio file.' when transcriptText is empty/undefined and input.audio?.contentBase64 is absent. Proves the core required-payload guard fires rather than persisting an empty note.

title: Create voice note transcript exactly at 12000-char limit
rationale: MAX_TRANSCRIPT_CHARS=12000; normalizeTranscript only throws when normalized.length > 12000. A 10,000-char {{LONG}} is under the cap and must be accepted (201). Confirms the boundary is exclusive '>' not '>=' and a long-but-legal transcript is stored.

title: Create voice note transcript far over 12000-char limit
rationale: normalizeTranscript throws 'Voice note transcript is too long. Keep it under 12000 characters.' once the whitespace-collapsed length exceeds 12000. A 100,000-char {{HUGE}} body (also near/under the 8MB http limit) must be rejected with the length message, not a 500.

title: Create voice note with a PAN in the transcript
rationale: assertNoRawPaymentCardData(transcriptText,'Voice note transcript') runs before persistence; {{PAN}}=4111111111111111 is Luhn-valid with MII 4, so containsLikelyPaymentCardNumber returns true and the PCI message 'Voice note transcript appears to contain payment card data...' is thrown. Verifies the PCI boundary on free-text transcript.

title: PAN obfuscated with spaces/dashes in transcript still rejected
rationale: PAN_CANDIDATE allows single hyphen/space separators between digit groups and strips them before the Luhn/MII check, so a dash-formatted Visa PAN is still detected. Confirms obfuscated card numbers cannot bypass the transcript PCI guard.

title: Create voice note with invalid contextType enum
rationale: inferContextType returns the supplied 'warehouse'; toPrismaContext finds no mapping in contextToPrisma and throws 'Unsupported voice note context type: warehouse'. Only general|lead|account|training_session|consignment_site|route_visit are valid. Proves enum rejection rather than a silent default.

title: Create voice note with whitespace-only transcript and no audio
expectMessageContains: requires either a transcript or an audio file
rationale: normalizeTranscript collapses \s+ and trims, yielding undefined for whitespace-only input; with no audio the empty-payload guard then throws. Confirms blank/whitespace transcripts are treated as no content, not stored as an empty note.

title: Create voice note with emoji/unicode transcript
bodyJson: {"contextType":"general","transcriptText":"Great visit 😀🚀 café déjà vu — 日本語 メモ"}
rationale: Transcript is free text with only length + PCI checks; multibyte unicode/emoji contains no Luhn-valid PAN and is under the char cap, so it must persist cleanly (201) and round-trip without corruption or 500.

title: Create voice note with SQL/script payload in transcript
rationale: Transcript is persisted via Prisma parameterized writes; the SQL/script string is data, not executed. A correct system stores it safely and returns 201 (no 500, no DB error). Verifies injection-safe handling of free text.

title: Create voice note title over 140 chars is truncated, not rejected
rationale: normalizeTitle slices to 140 chars rather than throwing. A 10,000-char title must be accepted and silently truncated, returning 201 with a <=140-char title. Confirms title length is a clamp, not a validation error.

title: Create voice note against a nonexistent accountId
rationale: assertContextAccess calls getAccountDetail; a well-formed but nonexistent/invisible accountId returns null and throws 'Account is not available for this mobile user.' The route catch maps thrown errors to 400. Confirms context linkage is validated against the actor's book.

title: Create voice note against a nonexistent trainingSessionId
rationale: assertContextAccess does prisma.trainingSession.findUnique and throws 'Training session was not found.' when null. The catch returns 400. Verifies training-context FK existence is enforced at create.

title: Create voice note against a nonexistent consignmentSiteId
rationale: assertContextAccess does prisma.consignmentSite.findUnique and throws 'Consignment site was not found.' when null. Confirms the consignment-context FK is validated; a bogus site id cannot anchor a note.

title: Create voice note with unsupported audio mime type
rationale: storeAudioIfPresent lowercases mimeType and rejects anything not in ALLOWED_AUDIO_MIME_TYPES with 'Unsupported voice note audio type: text/plain'. Verifies the audio MIME allow-list is enforced.

title: Create voice note with audio that decodes to empty bytes
rationale: Buffer.from('','base64').byteLength is 0, so storeAudioIfPresent throws 'Voice note audio must decode to a non-empty file.' Confirms empty/garbage base64 with a valid mime is still rejected before storage.

title: Create voice note with an invalid recordedAt date
expectMessageContains: recordedat must be a valid iso date
rationale: parseOptionalDate does new Date(value) and throws 'recordedAt must be a valid ISO date.' when getTime() is NaN. Verifies malformed timestamps are rejected rather than silently defaulted.

title: Create voice note with a far-future recordedAt
rationale: parseOptionalDate only validates that the date is parseable; there is no future-bound check, so a syntactically valid far-future ISO date is accepted (201). Documents that no future-date business rule exists on recordedAt — the boundary is parseability only.

title: SALES_BD_REP denied create on mobile voice notes (no mobile module)
rationale: POST /mobile/voice-notes calls requireAuthenticatedActor(req,{module:'mobile'}); ROLE_DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS for SALES_BD_REP excludes 'mobile', so assertModuleAccess throws an AuthorizationError mapped to 403. Verifies the mobile module gate denies non-field roles.

title: DEALER denied create on mobile voice notes
rationale: DEALER (DEALER_PORTAL_USER) has module access only to home/calendar/dealer_portal/notifications, never 'mobile', so the module gate denies create with 403. Confirms portal/dealer users cannot capture field voice notes.

title: FINANCE denied create (no mobile module) but allowed review-queue (has lead.view)
rationale: FINANCE module access list excludes 'mobile', so create is denied 403 even though FINANCE holds 'lead.view' (which would pass assertCanUseReviewQueue on the separate review-queue route). Confirms module gate and review-action gate are independent.

title: DEALER denied review-queue listing
expectMessageContains: dealer users cannot review field activity
rationale: listMobileVoiceNoteReviewQueue calls assertCanUseReviewQueue which throws 'Dealer users cannot review field activity.' for actor.actorType==='dealer'. This is a thrown Error (not an AuthorizationError class), so the http catch maps it to 400; 403 is also acceptable if the harness treats the deny semantically. Confirms dealers are blocked from the review surface.

title: Get voice note detail for a nonexistent id returns 404
rationale: GET /mobile-voice-notes/:id calls getMobileVoiceNoteDetail; a well-formed but nonexistent UUID yields findUnique null, the handler returns notFoundResponse(res,'Voice note was not found.') (404). Verifies detail not-found maps to a true 404 (distinct from the review POST 400 path).

title: Review a nonexistent voice note id
rationale: reviewMobileVoiceNote does findUnique then throws 'Voice note was not found.' when null. Unlike the detail GET, this is a thrown Error caught by the route and returned as 400. Documents the asymmetry: review of a missing note is a 400, not 404.

title: Review with malformed (non-UUID) voice note id
rationale: A syntactically invalid id ('not-a-uuid') reaches prisma.mobileVoiceNote.findUnique on a uuid column; Prisma raises a validation/cast error caught by the route as 400 (or surfaced as not-found). Confirms a malformed id is handled gracefully, never a 500.

title: Review with an invalid decision value
expectMessageContains: decision must be approve or reject
rationale: normalizeReviewDecision throws 'Review decision must be approve or reject.' for any value other than approve|reject. Verifies the decision enum is strictly validated before any state change.

title: Reject a voice note without notes or rejection reason
expectMessageContains: requires a review note or rejection reason
rationale: When decision==='reject' and both normalized reviewNotes and rejectedReason are empty, the service throws 'Rejecting a voice note requires a review note or rejection reason.' Verifies a rejection must carry justification.

title: Reject with a follow-up writeback action that is not activity_only
rationale: The service throws 'Follow-up actions are only available when approving a voice note.' when decision==='reject' and writebackAction is set to anything other than activity_only. Confirms follow-up creation is gated to the approve path.

title: Reject with a PAN in the rejection reason
rationale: reviewMobileVoiceNote calls assertNoRawPaymentCardData(rejectedReason,'Voice note rejection reason') before the empty-reason check; a Luhn-valid Visa PAN triggers 'Voice note rejection reason appears to contain payment card data...'. Verifies PCI guard covers reviewer-supplied free text, not just transcripts.

title: Approve with an unsupported writebackAction
rationale: normalizeReviewWritebackAction accepts only activity_only|create_training_follow_up|create_consignment_work_item and throws 'Unsupported voice note review action: create_account_task' otherwise. Verifies the writeback-action enum is validated on approve.

title: Re-review (idempotency/double-decision) an already-reviewed note
rationale: reviewMobileVoiceNote throws 'Voice note has already been reviewed.' unless reviewStatus===PENDING_REVIEW. Harness should first approve {{voiceNoteId}}, then replay the same review; the second call must be rejected. Confirms the review is a one-shot transition (no double-approve / no re-decision).

title: List voice notes with an over-max limit is clamped, not rejected
rationale: clampLimit floors/min-caps to MAX_LIMIT=100 (and falls back to DEFAULT_LIMIT=25 for <1). An out-of-range limit must return 200 with at most 100 items, not an error. Verifies pagination limit is sanitized server-side.

title: List voice notes with a non-numeric limit query param
rationale: readIntegerQuery returns undefined for a non-numeric 'abc'; clampLimit then defaults to 25. The request must succeed (200) with the default page size rather than 400/500. Confirms bad query types degrade gracefully to defaults.

title: TRAINING_OPS denied create (no mobile module)
rationale: TRAINING_OPS module access excludes 'mobile' (home/calendar/training/product_management/digital_assets/reports/notifications/settings), so the module gate denies create with 403 — even though TRAINING_OPS holds 'training.schedule' and could read the review-queue. Confirms create is mobile-module-only.

title: Login with empty body returns 401 (email and password required)
rationale: loginWithPassword normalizes email and trims password; if either is falsy it throws 'Email and password are required'. The login handler wraps every throw in unauthorizedResponse, so a missing-field login is a 401, never a 200. Proves required-field enforcement plus the handler's uniform 401 mapping.

title: Login with email but no password returns 401
rationale: password?.trim() is undefined when password key is absent, so the !password guard fires before any DB lookup. Confirms password is mandatory and that the absence is reported as the generic required message (401), not an invalid-credentials path.

title: Login with whitespace-only password is treated as empty and returns 401
rationale: password is trimmed via input.password?.trim(); a whitespace-only password collapses to '' and trips the required-field guard rather than the credential-comparison branch. Verifies trimming boundary on the password before verifySecret runs.

title: Login with unknown email returns 401 invalid email or password
rationale: When userIdentity.findFirst returns null, identity?.passwordHash is undefined and the guard throws the generic 'Invalid email or password'. The message must NOT distinguish unknown-email from wrong-password (anti-enumeration). Confirms uniform credential-error wording.

title: Login with known email but wrong password returns identical 401 message
rationale: verifySecret returns false for a wrong password, throwing the same 'Invalid email or password' as the unknown-email case. Pairing with AUTH-EDGE-004 proves the error message is constant regardless of which factor failed (no user enumeration leak).

title: Login email is case-insensitive and trimmed (uppercase + padding still resolves identity)
rationale: normalizeEmail lowercases and trims before the loginEmail lookup, so an uppercased padded email still matches the stored identity and then fails on the wrong password (invalid email or password) rather than failing earlier with a required-field error. Proves case/whitespace normalization reaches the credential branch.

title: Login with SQL injection payload in email is handled safely (no 500)
rationale: Prisma parameterizes the loginEmail equality filter, so a SQL payload is just an unmatched string -> null identity -> 'Invalid email or password'. Must return 401, never 500 or a leaked SQL error. Confirms safe handling of injection in the email field.

title: Login with script payload in email is treated as plain text (no 500)
rationale: The email is only used as a lookup key and never rendered server-side; a script tag is an unmatched email producing the generic credential error. Verifies no 500 and no reflection of the raw markup in a way that breaks the JSON contract.

title: Login with a 100,000-char password is rejected without a 500
rationale: readJsonBody caps the raw body at 1,000,000 bytes; a 100KB password stays under the cap so the request parses, then scrypt rejects it as a wrong password (401 invalid credentials). Confirms an oversize-but-under-limit secret degrades to a normal auth failure, not a crash.

title: Request body exceeding the 1MB cap is rejected (login handler returns 401)
rationale: readTextBody throws 'Request body exceeds 1000000 bytes' once accumulated chunks pass the cap (~100 x 10KB = 1MB+). The login handler's catch maps any throw to unauthorizedResponse, so an oversize body is a controlled 401 rather than an unbounded buffer/500. Proves the request-size guard fires before JSON parsing.

title: Malformed JSON body on login is caught and returns 401, not 500
rationale: readJsonBody throws 'Invalid JSON body: ...' on JSON.parse failure; the login handler catch converts it to a 401. Confirms a syntactically broken payload is a graceful auth error, not an unhandled 500. (Harness must send this raw, not re-serialized.)

title: Login with non-string email type degrades to a safe 401
rationale: normalizeEmail calls email?.trim(); a numeric value has no .trim so the optional-chaining short-circuits paths differ — in practice a number throws on .trim() and is caught by the handler as a 401, or normalizes to '' and hits the required-field guard. Either way the endpoint must not 500. Proves wrong-type input is contained as a 401.

title: PAN-shaped string as login email is just an unknown account (401, no card leakage)
rationale: Auth has no free-text/notes field storing a card, so a PAN embedded in the email is treated as an unmatched lookup key yielding the generic credential error. Verifies a test PAN does not cause a 500 and is not echoed back; it simply fails closed as invalid credentials.

title: Forgot-password with empty body returns 400 email required
rationale: requestPasswordReset throws 'Email is required' when normalizeEmail yields ''. The forgot-password handler maps every throw to badRequestResponse (400). This is the only throwing path; all other outcomes return 200. Confirms the single 400 branch.

title: Forgot-password for an unknown email returns 200 suppressed (anti-enumeration)
expectMessageContains: if a matching local pulse account
rationale: When no LOCAL identity/user is found, the service returns the genericSuppressedResponse (accepted:true, delivery:'suppressed') with HTTP 200. A correct system must NOT 404 or reveal that the account is unknown. Proves account-enumeration protection on recovery.

title: Forgot-password is case-insensitive (uppercased unknown email still 200 suppressed)
expectMessageContains: if a matching local pulse account
rationale: normalizeEmail lowercases before the lookup, so casing does not change the suppressed-vs-eligible decision. A correct system returns the same 200 suppressed envelope as the lowercase variant. Confirms email normalization on the recovery path and uniform response shape.

title: Forgot-password with SQL payload in email returns 200 suppressed, no 500
expectMessageContains: if a matching local pulse account
rationale: Prisma parameterizes the loginEmail filter; the injection string is an unmatched email, so the service returns the suppressed 200 envelope. Must not 500 and must not reveal the lookup outcome. Confirms safe handling plus preserved anti-enumeration semantics under injection.

title: Reset-password with no token returns 400 token required
rationale: resetPassword throws 'Password reset token is required' when token?.trim() is falsy, and the handler maps it to 400. The token check runs before the password checks, so a missing token is reported first. Confirms ordering and the required-token guard.

title: Reset-password with token but no new password returns 400
rationale: After the token guard passes, nextPassword?.trim() falsy throws 'New password is required' (400). Verifies the second required-field guard fires before any DB token lookup occurs.

title: Reset-password with a 9-char new password is rejected (off-by-one below min 10)
rationale: nextPassword.length < 10 throws 'New password must be at least 10 characters long'. A 9-char value is exactly one below the boundary and must be rejected before token validation. Confirms the minimum-length boundary check (the < 10, not <= 10, comparison).

title: Reset-password with exactly 10 chars passes length check and fails on bad token
rationale: A 10-char password is exactly at the boundary so the length guard passes; the flow then hashes the token, finds no matching passwordResetToken, and throws 'Password reset link is invalid or has expired'. Proves 10 is accepted (length boundary inclusive) and that an unknown token yields the invalid/expired message rather than a length error.

title: Reset-password with a well-formed but nonexistent token returns 400 invalid/expired
rationale: findUnique on tokenHash returns null for any token that was never issued; the service throws the generic invalid-or-expired message and the handler returns 400 (not 404 — reset deliberately uses 400 for unknown tokens to avoid distinguishing 'never existed' from 'expired'). Confirms token-existence failure is masked as invalid/expired.

title: Reset-password with SQL payload as token returns 400 invalid/expired, no 500
rationale: The token is SHA-256 hashed before the findUnique lookup, so an injection string becomes a deterministic hash with no matching row. Must produce the generic 400 invalid/expired, never a 500 or a bypass. Confirms hashing + parameterization neutralize injection on the reset token.

title: Refresh with empty body returns 401 refreshToken required
rationale: refreshSession throws 'refreshToken is required' when refreshToken?.trim() is falsy, and the refresh handler maps every throw to unauthorizedResponse (401). Confirms the required-field guard and the 401 mapping for the refresh route.

title: Refresh with an unknown refresh token returns 401 invalid session
rationale: findUnique on the hashed refreshToken returns null for an unissued token; validateActiveSession throws 'Invalid session' which the handler returns as 401. A correct system never 200s or 404s an unknown refresh token. Confirms unknown-session handling on refresh.

title: Refresh with script payload as refresh token returns 401, no 500
rationale: The refresh token is SHA-256 hashed before lookup, so a script string is just a non-matching hash -> 'Invalid session' 401. Must not 500 or reflect the markup. Confirms safe handling of hostile input on the refresh token.

title: GET /auth/me with no Authorization header returns 401 missing bearer token
rationale: The /auth/me handler reads the bearer via readBearerToken; with no header it returns null and the handler responds 401 'Missing bearer token' before any DB call. Confirms the unauthenticated path is rejected with the specific missing-token message.

title: GET /auth/me with malformed Authorization scheme returns 401
rationale: readBearerToken requires a 'Bearer <token>' shape; a header like 'Basic abc' or 'Token xyz' (non-bearer scheme) yields null, so the handler reports 'Missing bearer token' (401). Harness should send Authorization: 'Basic Zm9vOmJhcg=='. Confirms scheme validation rejects non-bearer credentials.

title: GET /auth/me with a bearer token that matches no session returns 401 invalid session
rationale: resolveSessionByAccessToken hashes the token and findUnique returns null for an unissued value, so getCurrentSession returns null and the handler responds 401 'Invalid session'. Harness should send Authorization: 'Bearer {{nonexistentId}}'. Confirms a well-formed-but-unknown bearer is rejected, not treated as anonymous-OK.

title: POST /auth/logout without a bearer token returns 401
rationale: The logout handler reads the bearer first; absent it returns 401 'Missing bearer token' before parsing the body. Confirms logout requires authentication and rejects anonymous calls.

title: POST /auth/logout with a refreshToken in the body returns 400 (bearer-only logout)
rationale: After bearer validation, the logout handler explicitly rejects a body containing refreshToken with badRequestResponse 'Logout currently uses bearer access token only'. This requires a valid bearer to even reach the check, so the harness must supply a live access token for a QA fixture session. Confirms the documented bearer-only logout constraint.

title: Repeating logout for the same session twice both succeed (idempotent revoke)
rationale: logoutCurrentSession only writes a revocation when !session.revokedAt, but always returns {sessionId, revokedAt}. The FIRST logout with a valid QA fixture bearer returns 200; the access token remains hashed in the session row, so an immediate REPEAT still resolves the (now-revoked) session and returns 200 without a second write. Confirms logout is idempotent rather than erroring on an already-revoked session. (Use a freshly provisioned QA session token, never a seed account.)

title: Login attempt for a deactivated user is rejected with 401 user is inactive
rationale: After credentials verify, loginWithPassword checks identity.user.isActive and throws 'User is inactive' for a deactivated account, mapped to 401. This is a distinct state from invalid-credentials and must only surface AFTER the password matches (so it cannot be used to enumerate active accounts with a wrong password). Requires a QA fixture user that is correct-password but isActive=false.

title: Microsoft Entra start returns 503 when SSO is not configured
rationale: startMicrosoftEntraLogin calls requireConfiguredMicrosoftEntra, which throws MicrosoftEntraAuthUnavailableError unless tenantId+clientId+clientSecret+redirectUri are all set; the handler maps that error to serviceUnavailableResponse (503). In an environment without Entra env vars this is the grounded outcome. (If Entra IS configured in prod, a 200 with an authorizationUrl is the alternative correct response — but per the code the unconfigured branch returns 503.)

title: Microsoft Entra complete with missing code/state returns 503 (unconfigured) or 400 (configured)
rationale: completeMicrosoftEntraLogin first calls requireConfiguredMicrosoftEntra; if Entra is unconfigured the handler returns 503 before validation. If it IS configured, the missing code/state guard throws 'Missing Microsoft Entra authorization code or state' which the handler's regex maps to 400. Both are correct depending on env; the message always contains 'microsoft entra'. Confirms the configure-then-validate ordering.

title: Wrong HTTP method on /auth/login (GET) returns 405 with Allow: POST
rationale: The login route only accepts POST; any other method hits methodNotAllowedResponse which sets Allow: POST and returns 405. Confirms method gating is enforced per-route and that GET cannot reach the login logic.

title: Wrong HTTP method on /auth/me (POST) returns 405 with Allow: GET
rationale: /auth/me only accepts GET; a POST triggers methodNotAllowedResponse with Allow: GET (405). This check runs before the bearer-token read, so even an unauthenticated POST returns 405 rather than 401. Confirms method gating precedes auth on the me route.

title: Reusing a refresh token after it has been rotated returns 401
rationale: refreshSession rotates tokens: it overwrites refreshTokenHash with a new value inside the transaction. After one successful refresh, the OLD refresh token no longer hashes to any session row, so a replay (the harness provisions a QA session, refreshes once, then replays the original token) yields null -> 'Invalid session' 401. Confirms refresh-token rotation invalidates the prior token (replay protection).

title: Reset-password with a numeric newPassword is contained safely (400)
rationale: newPassword?.trim() on a number has no string .trim(); optional chaining does not guard a present-but-wrong-type value, so the call throws (e.g. trim is not a function) and the reset handler funnels every error to badRequestResponse (400). Verifies a wrong-typed password field is contained as a 400, never a 500. (A correct system could also normalize/validate type and return 400 with a clearer message.)

title: Reset-password accepts a 10+ char unicode/emoji password at the length boundary
rationale: The length guard uses JS string .length (UTF-16 code units); 'pâsswörd-🔐-Ω' exceeds 10 units so it passes the minimum check, and the flow then fails on the unknown token with 'invalid or has expired'. Confirms unicode/emoji passwords are not rejected by the length rule and that surrogate-pair handling does not cause a 500.

title: PAN in lead activity note is rejected with payment-card message
rationale: pci.ts containsLikelyPaymentCardNumber matches 4111111111111111 (16 digits, MII 4 in [2-6], Luhn-valid). leads/service.ts logLeadActivityNote calls assertNoRawPaymentCardData(noteText,'Note text'), which throws the PCI_REJECTION_SUFFIX message; http maps service errors to 400. Proves the defense-in-depth free-text PAN guard fires.

title: 12-digit number is below PAN length floor and must NOT be PCI-rejected
rationale: pci.ts requires digits.length>=13. A 12-digit value (even MII 4) fails the length guard, so containsLikelyPaymentCardNumber returns false and the note saves. Confirms the lower boundary off-by-one: 12 digits is not treated as a card.

title: 19-digit Luhn-valid card-prefixed number hits the PAN length ceiling and is rejected
rationale: pci.ts accepts length 13-19. 4035501000000008147 is 19 digits, MII 4, Luhn-valid, so it is within the inclusive upper bound and must be rejected. Proves the 19-digit ceiling is inclusive.

title: 20-digit number exceeds PAN ceiling and must NOT be PCI-rejected
rationale: pci.ts caps PAN length at 19 (digits.length<=19). A 20-digit run is rejected by the length guard, so the note is allowed. Confirms the upper boundary off-by-one above 19 digits.

title: Non-card MII (number starting with 1) is not flagged as a PAN
rationale: pci.ts requires /^[2-6]/ on the digit string. A Luhn-valid 16-digit value starting with 1 (timestamp-like) fails the MII test, so it is not a PAN. Proves MII gating excludes the millisecond-timestamp false positive the comment calls out.

title: Amex-style 15-digit MII-3 PAN is rejected
rationale: pci.ts MII test /^[2-6]/ includes 3 (Amex/Diners/JCB). 378282246310005 is 15 digits, MII 3, Luhn-valid, within 13-19 length, so it must be rejected. Proves MII 3 boundary is covered, not just Visa MII 4.

title: PAN obfuscated with zero-width spaces is still rejected
rationale: pci.ts strips INVISIBLE_FORMATTING (incl. U+200B) before matching, so a PAN split by zero-width spaces collapses to 16 contiguous digits and is rejected. Proves the copy-paste-artifact bypass is closed.

title: PAN with dash separators between groups is rejected
rationale: pci.ts PAN_CANDIDATE allows a single hyphen separator between digit groups; the digits are then stripped to 16 contiguous Luhn-valid MII-4 digits. Proves dash-formatted PANs are caught, not just contiguous ones.

title: Comma-separated digit list is NOT concatenated into a false-positive PAN
rationale: pci.ts PAN_CANDIDATE deliberately EXCLUDES comma as a separator (it is list punctuation). The four 4-digit groups stay separate, none reaches 13 digits, so no PAN is detected and the note saves. Proves the comma exclusion that avoids CSV false positives.

title: PAN typed into any field of the public CIS form is rejected before persist
rationale: cis/service.ts submitPublicCis runs assertNoRawPaymentCardDataInRecord(mergedForm,'The CIS form'), which scans every string value one level deep. A PAN in a non-card-named field must still be refused. Proves record-level scan, not just named fields. (Public route is token-auth; role here is illustrative for the harness.)

title: FINANCE is denied admin audit-log read (default-deny on unmapped action)
rationale: ROLE_DEFAULT_ACTION_ACCESS.FINANCE does not include admin.audit_view (only EXECUTIVE, SUPER_ADMIN, SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP, ADMIN_CSR_OPS have it). admin/http withAdminAuth requires admin.audit_view; assertActionAccess throws AuthorizationError -> 403. Proves default-deny for an unmapped action.

title: SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP IS permitted admin audit-log read
rationale: ROLE_DEFAULT_ACTION_ACCESS.SALES_BD_LEADERSHIP explicitly includes admin.audit_view and module admin. Positive RBAC control: confirms a mapped role is allowed where the FINANCE case is denied, so a 403 in CROS-EDGE-011 is a genuine deny, not a blanket block.

title: EXECUTIVE (read-only, hardened) is denied admin user creation
rationale: auth.ts comment: EXECUTIVE was hardened 2026-06-22 to oversight/read only; ROLE_DEFAULT_ACTION_ACCESS.EXECUTIVE omits admin.user_manage. admin/http POST /admin/users requires admin.user_manage -> assertActionAccess throws -> 403. Proves the executive write-lockdown.

title: DEALER role is denied all internal lead reads (tightly bounded portal access)
rationale: ROLE_DEFAULT_MODULE_ACCESS.DEALER_PORTAL_USER is only [home,calendar,dealer_portal,notifications] and its action list has no lead.view. assertModuleAccess('leads') fails first -> AuthorizationError -> 403. Proves the dealer is fenced out of internal CRM modules.

title: TERRITORY_MANAGER is denied finance decisioning on a CIS package
rationale: cis/service.ts recordFinanceDecision asserts lead.finance_decide, which only FINANCE and SUPER_ADMIN hold in ROLE_DEFAULT_ACTION_ACCESS. TM lacks it -> AuthorizationError -> 403. Proves finance decisioning is locked to the finance role.

title: SALES_BD_REP is denied the Widen manifest sync action
rationale: digital-assets/http requires digital_asset.sync for widen-import-preview; ROLE_DEFAULT_ACTION_ACCESS grants sync only to ADMIN_CSR_OPS and SUPER_ADMIN (SUPER_ADMIN excludes only consignment.sync). SALES_BD_REP lacks digital_asset.sync -> 403. Proves the sync action is privileged.

title: Directory-traversal manifest path is rejected as outside the manifest root
rationale: digital-assets/service.ts resolveManifestPathWithinRoot resolves against the widen-manifests subdir and throws 'Widen manifest path resolved outside the configured manifest directory' when the resolved path escapes baseDir. Run as an allowed sync role so the 400 proves the traversal guard, not RBAC.

title: Absolute manifest path is contained to the manifest subdir (no arbitrary file read)
rationale: resolveManifestPathWithinRoot strips leading separators (/^[/\\]+/) so an absolute path is treated as relative to baseDir; /etc/shadow becomes baseDir/etc/shadow, which does not exist -> readFile ENOENT surfaces as a 400 service error, and the process never reads the real /etc/shadow. Proves absolute paths cannot escape the storage root.

title: SQL/script payload in a lead note is stored safely, not executed or 500
rationale: Notes persist via Prisma parameterized writes (leads/service.ts logLeadActivityNote -> prisma.create) with no raw SQL or HTML rendering. The payload contains no PAN, so it is stored verbatim and returns 201. Proves injection text is handled safely rather than crashing (no 500) or being executed.

title: Empty lead note text is rejected by the required-field check
rationale: leads/service.ts: noteText = optionalTrimmed(input.note) ?? ''; if (!noteText) throw new Error('Note text is required'). Whitespace trims to empty and triggers the guard before any persistence. Proves required-field enforcement on the note body.

title: Oversize lead note body is bounded by the request size limit
rationale: utils/http.ts readTextBody enforces maxBytes (1,000,000) and throws 'Request body exceeds N bytes'. A {{HUGE}} 100k-char note inside a larger payload approaches/exceeds that ceiling; oversize bodies must be refused rather than processed. Proves request-size bounding at the boundary.

title: Unicode/emoji note text is accepted and stored (no PAN, no crash)
bodyJson: {"note":"Met owner ñame 🚀你好 follow up next week"}
rationale: pci.ts only flags Luhn-valid card-prefixed digit runs; non-digit unicode/emoji are irrelevant. The note has no PAN and is persisted via Prisma with utf8 handling. Proves multibyte/emoji input is processed cleanly, returning 201 not 500.

title: Lead note on a well-formed but nonexistent lead returns 404
rationale: leads/service.ts logLeadActivityNote does prisma.lead.findUnique and throws `Lead not found: ${leadId}` when null. RBAC passes (SALES_BD_REP has lead.intake_manage), so a well-formed UUID that does not exist must surface as 404, not 403/500.

title: Malformed (non-UUID) lead id on note route is rejected, not treated as found
rationale: The :leadId segment 'not-a-uuid' reaches prisma.lead.findUnique; a syntactically invalid UUID either yields no row (404 'Lead not found') or a Prisma validation error mapped to 400. A correct system must not 500 or treat it as an existing lead. Proves malformed-id handling distinct from the nonexistent-but-valid case.

title: Missing bearer token on a protected route returns 401 before any RBAC check
rationale: auth/request.ts requireAuthenticatedActor: readBearerToken returns undefined with no Authorization header -> throws AuthenticationError('Missing bearer token') -> 401, before assertModuleAccess/assertActionAccess run. Proves authentication precedes authorization (executor must omit the token for this case).

title: PAN inside a voice-note rejection reason is rejected at review time
rationale: mobile-voice-notes/service.ts review path calls assertNoRawPaymentCardData(rejectedReason,'Voice note rejection reason'). The {{PAN}} (MII 4, Luhn-valid, 16 digits) trips the guard and the review is refused. Proves PCI enforcement on the transcript/review surface, not only CIS/leads notes.

title: Finance decision on a CIS package not in a finance-review state is rejected
rationale: cis/service.ts recordFinanceDecision: if status not in {FINANCE_PENDING, FINANCE_APPROVED, FINANCE_DECLINED} it throws 'CIS package is not in a finance-review state'. A freshly issued/draft package fails this transition. Proves the finance state-machine gate (target a QA fixture package not yet submitted to finance).

title: Invalid finance decision enum value is rejected
rationale: cis/service.ts mapFinanceDecisionState/validateFinanceDecisionInput only recognise approved/declined/requested-info style decisions; 'maybe' is not a mapped decision and must be rejected with a validation error rather than silently applied. Proves enum validation on the decision field.

title: Repeating an approved finance decision does not double-apply or 500
rationale: recordFinanceDecision allows status FINANCE_APPROVED to be re-decided (upsert on financeDecision), so a repeat approve either returns 200 with the same terminal state or is rejected by validateFinanceDecisionInput. Either way it must be deterministic, not produce a duplicate/500. Proves idempotent re-submission behaviour on the mutation.

title: Audit activity limit query is clamped, not trusted verbatim
rationale: admin/service.ts listAdminActivity uses take: Math.min(100, Math.max(1, input.limit ?? 20)). An over-large limit is clamped to 100 rather than fetching unbounded rows. Run as SUPER_ADMIN (has admin.audit_view) so 200 with a bounded page proves pagination clamping.

title: Non-numeric audit limit query does not break the listing
rationale: admin/http does limit=Number('abc') -> NaN; listAdminActivity take: Math.min(100, Math.max(1, NaN ?? 20)) — NaN is not undefined so Math.max(1,NaN)=NaN and Math.min(100,NaN)=NaN. A correct system must still return a valid page (clamp/ignore) rather than 500. Probes bad query-param robustness on the audit endpoint.

title: Unknown/garbage role string is rejected (default-deny on unmapped role)
rationale: auth/guards.ts normalizeRole throws AuthorizationError('Unknown role: ...') for any value not in AUTH_ROLES or ROLE_ALIASES, and ROLE_DEFAULT_*_ACCESS has no entry for an unmapped role. A session/role outside the known set must be denied (403) or treated as unauthenticated (401), never granted access. Proves the system fails closed on unrecognised roles.
